name: Phase-level timeout with auto-escalation
hypothesis: Some iterations run 30-40 minutes because the configured invocation timeout (600s) is not enforced with a context deadline. Enforcing a 15-minute hard timeout per Claude invocation and auto-escalating to the next tier will cap wasted time on stuck iterations, reducing p95 iteration duration from ~35min to <18min without significantly increasing cost (the escalated attempt replaces time that would have been wasted).
change: In the invoker, wrap each Claude invocation with context.WithTimeout using a configurable phase timeout (default 900s / 15min). When the timeout fires, classify it as phase_timeout and let the existing escalation handler route it to the next tier. Add a log line when phase timeout fires to make data collection explicit.
measurement: Track: (1) count of iterations hitting phase timeout, (2) success rate of the escalated attempt after timeout, (3) p95 iteration duration before vs after, (4) total wall-clock time per bead. Success criteria: p95 duration <18min AND escalated-attempt success rate >30%. Danger signal: if escalated attempts have <30% success, the timeout is adding cost without reducing total time.
risk: Some legitimately complex beads need >15 minutes (e.g., cross-package refactors). A hard timeout could cause unnecessary escalation for beads that would have succeeded with a few more minutes. The escalated attempt on a higher tier adds ~$0.79 per opus escalation. If false positive rate is high, total cost increases. Mitigation: 15min is well above the ~8min average, so only true outliers get cut off.
